correctness.rationale: Any nonempty antipalindromic subsequence has opposite end bits and equal-length complementary mirror runs. A cut of the circle has at most five runs, so the subsequence has two or four. In the two-run case both colors cannot use both of their source runs: those four source runs alternate in circular order. Thus one color contributes at most one run, and all four candidate capacities are achieved by choosing a boundary cut and skipping the intervening unwanted run. A four-run subsequence uses all four source runs: omission leaves at most two circular color transitions. With all four used, the circular runs of the subsequence correspond one-to-one to the original ones; a split source run cannot contribute at both linear ends, since those ends are opposite. The two possible adjacent pairings give the two terms of Q. In the balanced case the exact half-length is max(s/2+U,s-U+V), where U and V are respectively the larger and smaller absolute deviations of a and b from s/2. Averaging gives 3s/4+V/2, and integrality gives the ceiling. In the stated construction s=4m+r, U=m+r/2 and V is 0 or 1/2, so both terms are at most 3m+r and the first equals it. The s=2,3 cases attain s. For 4 dividing s, equality forces V=0 and U=s/4, giving exactly the stated cyclic run profiles.
residual_risks: The archived finite checks were inspected, not rerun; correctness is established by the run and equality arguments rather than finite testing.
